#161031. Interest-Free Credit From Suppliers – Ask for Longer Terms and Pay on the Due Date

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (501 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

Interest-Free Credit From Suppliers – Ask for Longer Terms and Pay on the Due Date

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (501 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Supplier payment terms are credit that charges no interest, and every extra day you get keeps cash in your business.
  • It has been revealed that paying suppliers on delivery, or paying each invoice the day it arrives, hands over cash that terms would let you keep for weeks.
  • Recent findings suggest that terms like net 30 give you 30 days after the invoice date to pay the full bill, with no interest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Supplier payment terms are credit that charges no interest, and every extra day you get keeps cash in your business. Once you’ve paid a supplier on time for a few months, ask for 30 to 60 days to pay. Then pay each bill on its due date, not early, unless the supplier offers a discount for paying sooner.

It has been revealed that paying suppliers on delivery, or paying each invoice the day it arrives, hands over cash that terms would let you keep for weeks. That cash could be covering payroll, rent, or the next order.

Recent findings suggest that terms like net 30 give you 30 days after the invoice date to pay the full bill, with no interest. Take a gift shop that buys about $12,000 a month from its two biggest suppliers and pays on delivery. Moving both to net 45 means it pays for each order a month and a half later, so about $18,000 more stays in its account going into the holiday season.

In a recent development, ask for longer terms after a few months of paying a supplier on time, since that record is your best argument. Go from paying on delivery to net 30, or from net 30 to net 45 or net 60. Better still, ask for terms that match how long your own customers take to pay you, so their payments come in by the time your bills come due.

Then pay on the due date, not before and never after, with each payment scheduled in your bank’s bill pay to arrive that day. Many suppliers report how you pay to Dun & Bradstreet, whose PAYDEX business credit score tracks how promptly you pay them. A late payment can pull that score down, and it gives a supplier reason to shorten your terms, not lengthen them.

The exception is a discount for paying early. Terms of 2/10 net 30 take 2% off a bill paid within 10 days and otherwise give you 30 days to pay it in full. Saving 2% for paying 20 days sooner is like earning about 37% a year on that money, far more than a savings account pays, so take the discount whenever you have the cash to spare. Offering your own customers an early-payment discount turns that 37% into a cost you pay.

Start with the supplier you pay the most, since every extra 30 days of terms keeps about one month’s worth of its bills in your account.

📖 Baca

U.S. Trio Make First Snowboard and Ski Descent of a Near-7,000'er in Langtang

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1118 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).
  • The team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style.
  • On the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).

The team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style. They summited on October 20 and rode/skied down via the same line on the south face, while American photographer Blake Gordon and Canadian cinematographer Leo Hoorn filmed from a high camp.

On the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026. Photo: Nick Russell.

“The south face of Dorje was always the goal, and I’d been planning/dreaming of it for over two years,” Nick Russell told ExplorersWeb while on his way to the airport.

The expedition reached base camp on October 6, shortly after an intense storm blanketed Nepal’s mountains with heavy snow. For them, however, the snow was a blessing rather than a curse.

“The cyclone gave our zone some much-needed snow down low, and on the face, it allowed a clean descent (no down climbing, no rappels),” Russell remarked.

Sickness slowed the beginning of the expedition. “Three out of five of us, myself included, caught COVID,” Russell noted. Luckily, the climbers recovered just as the weather cleared and winds dropped, followed by a string of perfect days.

Industry observers note that after the descent. Photo: Nick Russell/Instgram.

Industry observers note that “Adam, Billy, and I all carried our own gear, set the tracks, and climbed in alpine style on the face,” Nick Russell stated. The team had hired three Sherpa climbers (Dawa Geljee Sherpa, Kami Sherpa, and Nuri Sherpa) who helped the camera crew get their gear to a high camp, plus a base camp crew, outfitted by Shangri-La Nepal Trek.

In a recent development, high camp at 6,000m on the south face of Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

In a recent development, the line of ascent/descent followed the snow from below 4,500m to Camp 1 (4,900m) by crossing an icefall. According to the team, this was the only real crux of the ascent, due to overhead serac hazard. At least, the exposed section was short — less than an hour.

Recent findings suggest that on the first day of the summit push, the team continued to their high camp at 6,000m, below the col and at the base of the snowy face. Russell recalls the details of the climb as follows:.

Recent findings suggest that the south face is quite steep and sustained above the bergshrund, with sustained 45-50˚ and pockets of 55º, we estimate. The face had seen so much sun [over] the past two weeks that the rising conditions were the biggest unknown of the entire project.

In a recent development, we didn’t know whether or not it would be too icy to ride/ski until we got on the face. The snow was mostly firm, pretty much on the brink of being edge-able. It was two tool and crampon climbing the entire way, with no proper rests to take the pack off.

It took about 7.5 hours to climb the face, and we topped out around 1:30 pm. It took roughly 1.5 hours to descend, with breaks for the cameras to reset.

It has been revealed that A climber leaves almost no tracks in the hard snow on Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

It has been revealed that the three summiters started down from the top at the same time, Russell on snowboard and his partners on skis. It was anything but easy.

“The snow was more firm than I would have liked, but just edgeable enough to hold an edge,” Russell recalls. “Between the altitude, exposure below, steepness, and how firm it was, it was by far the heaviest line I’ve ever ridden.” He added that if the snow had been a little harder, they would have had to rappel down.

Sources indicate that the hard snow on the upper sections. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

It has been revealed that “You always hope for stable, boot-top powder, but that’s rarely the case at high altitude,” Russell explained. “Instead, you make the most of the conditions presented and try to do it as safely as possible.”.

He added: “The entire line was a no-fall zone; one lost edge, and it’d be over. Regardless of conditions, it was a dream for all of us to ride off the top of a peak in Nepal.”.

It has been revealed that after a partial descent, the team spent the night at high camp, hoping to ride some interesting slopes they had spotted earlier, but finally decided to bail the next morning. “We were satisfied,” Russell said. They continued on skis/snowboard all the way down to the moraines below Camp 1 around 4,500m.

Industry observers note that childhood friends Fabrikant and Haas often partner up on major ski expeditions, mainly in Alaska but also in the Himalaya. They climbed and skied both Gasherbrums 1 and 2 without oxygen after climbing them in the same style in 2024, together with Brendan O’Neill.

“They are the strongest partners I’ve ever been in the mountains with,” noted Russell, who has also climbed and snowboarded twice in the Indian Himalaya and twice in Nepal.

“I tried Dhaulagiri in 2022 with Blake Gordon and Dan Corn, but the difficult conditions that year coupled with the loss of Hilaree Nelson [who fell to her death while trying to ski down Manaslu] didn’t allow us to make very much progress,” Russell stated.

“I’ve always dreamed of riding lines in the Himalaya, and this felt like a major step forward in my personal journey,” he concluded.

While this is the first ski and snowboard descent of Dorje Lhakpa’s south face, the legendary Marco Siffredi snowboarded the west ridge of the mountain in 1999, with Bertrand Delapierre. Siffredi perished shortly afterward on the Hornbein Couloir on Mount Everest. “Dorje Lhakpa first entered my psyche from Marco and Bertrand’s descent,” the rider recalled.

The south face of Dorje Lhakpa was only climbed for the first time in 2021, by Spaniards Mikel Inoriza, Iker Madoz, and Mikel Zabalza.

“I came across a photo of the south face and the American Alpine Journal article from the Spanish team’s first ascent in 2021,” Russell remarked. “The massive south face is visible from the Kathmandu Valley on a clear day, and it is honestly crazy to me that no one had skied it before.”.

“Today,” he went on, “people are so hyper-focused on the 8,000m peaks (for good reason, I get it), but there are still virgin lines waiting for a snowboard/ski descent in the 6,000-7,000m range. It just takes a shit ton of work to make it happen.”.

Saddle to Paddle: Bikerafting From Canada to Mexico

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pete Streufert and his friend Carter (no last name) are cycling 4,025km and packrafting 645km across the U.S.
  • Their route connects the rivers with long-distance cycling trails.
  • Before starting the journey on September 17, he mentioned they could find no record of anyone using this particular combination of rivers and cycling routes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pete Streufert and his friend Carter (no last name) are cycling 4,025km and packrafting 645km across the U.S. from Canada to Mexico. Starting in Glacier National Park, they will cross four rivers and six U.S. states to finish in El Paso, Texas.

Their route connects the rivers with long-distance cycling trails. This allows the pair to cross landscapes that would usually require separate trips by bike and watercraft. Streufert, a geospatial wildfire scientist and cartographer, came up with the route by combining existing GPS tracks and geographical data from Bikepacking.com, American Whitewater, and OpenStreetMap. He overlaid cycling corridors and rivers to identify where the two could connect.

Before starting the journey on September 17, he mentioned they could find no record of anyone using this particular combination of rivers and cycling routes. So it is possible that they are the first to do so.

Industry observers note that they started what they neatly call the Saddle to Paddle Traverse on September 17, from Glacier National Park, Montana, on the Canadian border. They kicked off the first packrafting section with a 115km descent of the North Fork of the Flathead River, which forms part of the western boundary of Glacier National Park.

In a recent development, from there, they followed the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route through Montana toward Jackson Lake, Wyoming, for 1,107km. Here, they hit their second paddling phase on the Snake River.

Every time they reach a river, the pair inflates their rafts, load their bicycles aboard, and paddle downstream. Then at each takeout, they deflate the rafts, attach them to their bikes, and continue riding.

It has been revealed that the route. Photo: Pete Streufert.

Industry observers note that after 130km along the Snake River, their route joined the SLoToJa cycling corridor. They pedaled through Idaho, Wyoming, and Utah. Here, a short connector track took them onto the newly developed Golden Gravel Trail. A further 860km of cycling brought them to Utah’s Green River.

They then paddled 328km through Desolation and Gray Canyons, including a handful of Class III rapids, and their only Class IV rapid of the trip.

Pulling their rafts out in Canyonlands National Park, they took the White Rim Trail to Moab. They are now taking a few days in Moab to “get all the mud off our bikes and escape the rain for a day or two before we keep heading south,” claims Streufert.

From here, they will once again pick up the Golden Gravel Trail through the La Sal Mountains and across Colorado, then continue on the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route to New Mexico.

Paddling the Green River. Photo: Pete Streufert.

A final paddling section on New Mexico’s Rio Chama will take them to the last leg of the trip, a 950km ride to El Paso.

The pair are riding Rodeo Labs Flaanimal 6.0 Steel, fitted with 29-inch Vittoria Mezcal tires, and using Kokopelli packrafts. The pair have described this as a “self-supported” route, although of course they’re replenishing their food along the way. They seem to combine camping with staying in towns.

View this post on Instagram See this post on Instagram.

They should complete the journey within the next few weeks, within their two-month timeline. You can follow their progress here.

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (390 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

Bailing Someone Out? Pay the Court – A Bondsman Keeps Its Fee

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (390 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that if you can afford a loved one’s bail, pay it in full to the court.
  • In a recent development, say a judge sets $5,000 bail, the charges are later dismissed, and the court deducts nothing.
  • It has been revealed that the court holds the cash until the case is over, which can take months, and some courts keep part of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you can afford a loved one’s bail, pay it in full to the court. The money comes back when the case ends, as long as they make every court date, minus any fees or fines the court deducts. A bail bondsman’s fee, usually 10% of the bail, is gone even if the charges are dropped.

In a recent development, say a judge sets $5,000 bail, the charges are later dismissed, and the court deducts nothing. A mother who paid her son’s bail in cash gets all $5,000 back, while a neighbor who paid a bondsman the usual 10% fee on the same amount is out $500 for good.

It has been revealed that the court holds the cash until the case is over, which can take months, and some courts keep part of it. Newly introduced York keeps 3% of it after a conviction, and Florida first withholds any unpaid court costs and fines the defendant owes. Even that 3% is less than a third of a bondsman’s usual 10% fee.

Sources indicate that A bondsman gives the court a written promise to pay the full bail if the defendant misses court, and the fee pays for that promise. Whoever pays the fee usually signs as the cosigner, on the hook for that full amount, so the fee isn’t the most you can lose. The bondsman may also hold collateral against that debt, such as your car’s title or a lien on your house.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A 26-year-old Australian solo trekker who fell from a cliff near Lobuche in the Everest region has been evacuated by helicopter to Kathmandu. He is recovering in intensive care. By law, all foreign trekkers are supposed to have a guide in the Khumbu.

In a recent development, joshua Patrick Cherubino sustained severe head injuries after falling at Kongma La Pass. He was first taken to Lobuche, then flown out on October 27, according to The Tourism Times.

Kongma La, at about 5,535m, is the highest of the trio of high passes on the classic Everest Three Passes circuit. It links the Chhukung side of the Imja Valley with Lobuche over rocky, non-glaciated moraine. The crossing is long and remote; the descent toward Lobuche is often loose underfoot and comes after hours already spent at altitude.

Industry observers note that the case has again drawn attention to Nepal’s rules in the Khumbu. Since 2023, the Nepal Tourism Board has required that all foreign trekkers be accompanied by a licensed guide within national parks, including Sagarmatha.

In practice, the local Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality has continued to issue its own permits and has not strictly enforced the national guide requirement. Thus, independent trekking remains common on the main Everest routes. Officials quoted by The Tourism Times described unguided travel in the region as a violation of the mandatory rule and a source of preventable rescues.

Sources indicate that cherubino was traveling alone when he was found. No further details on the circumstances of the fall or his condition have been released beyond the hospital’s assessment that he is recovering.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With a Section 8 tenant, the local housing authority pays its share of the rent straight to you, but only for a unit that passes its inspection at a rent it approves.
  • HUD’s fact sheet for landlords promises timely payments and says voucher tenants stay in a unit seven to eight years on average.
  • The tenant usually pays 30% of their income after deductions toward rent and utilities, and the authority pays the rest, up to its payment standard, the most it pays for a unit that size.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With a Section 8 tenant, the local housing authority pays its share of the rent straight to you, but only for a unit that passes its inspection at a rent it approves. Check your state and local law before you decide, since many states and cities bar turning down an applicant for paying with a voucher.

HUD’s fact sheet for landlords promises timely payments and says voucher tenants stay in a unit seven to eight years on average.

The tenant usually pays 30% of their income after deductions toward rent and utilities, and the authority pays the rest, up to its payment standard, the most it pays for a unit that size. The tenant pays any rent above the standard, but at move-in their share can’t top 40% of their income after deductions.

It has been revealed that take a tenant with no deductions, in a unit whose rent includes utilities and falls within the standard. Earning $24,000 a year, they pay 30% of $2,000 a month, or $600, and on a $1,600 rent the authority sends you the other $1,000.

Before payments start, you sign a contract with the authority, add HUD’s tenancy addendum to your lease, and pass its inspection. A failed item means repairs and a recheck, often while the unit sits empty. Inspectors return at least every two years, or every three at a small rural authority. They use HUD’s Housing Quality Standards or the newer NSPIRE standard, which a July 2026 HUD notice tells every authority to adopt by Feb. 1, 2027.

According to recent reports, the authority also limits your rent to what similar unsubsidized units rent for. The addendum bars an increase during the lease’s first term and requires 60 days’ notice to the authority before a later one, which it checks against similar units too. So the program suits a unit that’s already in good repair and priced near local market rents.

According to recent reports, the authority’s payments depend on federal funding, which can run late. After the 2025 government shutdown, Georgia’s Department of Community Affairs didn’t pay landlords the rest of November’s housing assistance until Dec. 5. Under the addendum, you can’t charge the tenant the authority’s share or evict them over its late payment.

Sources indicate that the Poverty & Race Research Action Council lists the state and local laws that protect voucher holders. Where one covers your rental, screen voucher holders by the same written standard you use for every applicant.

West Ridge or Hornbein Couloir? Everest Team Prepares for Fourth Attempt

📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (629 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Russian team is preparing to head up Everest’s West Ridge for a fourth time.
  • According to recent reports, andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening.
  • Recent findings suggest that “So far, we have completed three rotations on the mountain,” leader Vasiliev told ExplorersWeb.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Russian team is preparing to head up Everest’s West Ridge for a fourth time. While no easy option exists, they want to avoid the extremely exposed, difficult, and uncertain ridge route. Their only alternative is the Hornbein Couloir, which would force them to stray temporarily into Tibet.

According to recent reports, andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening. They will return to their base in Lobuche this weekend, determined to climb Everest without supplemental oxygen.

Everest West Ridge some days ago. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Recent findings suggest that “So far, we have completed three rotations on the mountain,” leader Vasiliev told ExplorersWeb. “Part of this time was spent exploring different options for accessing the route.”.

The Russian team has a permit to climb Everest from Nepal, as long as they attempt a route other than the standard Khumbu Icefall-South Col-Southeast Ridge. This has become the normal South Side route since Hillary and Tenzing’s first ascent in 1953.

Topo of the Russian team’s planned route on Everest, courtesy of Andrei Vasiliev.

First, the Russians tried to bypass the Khumbu Icefall via the Nuptse Shoulder toward Camp 1, but heavy snow forced them to find another route. Crossing the Icefall (sharing paths with the normal route) was also too hard in the deep snow and on the shaky snow bridges over the innumerable crevasses.

Industry observers note that “Eventually, we selected a third option, via the Lho La,” Vasiliev mentioned. “From that pass, our planned route continues across the West Shoulder, along the West Ridge.”.

Sources indicate that at the Lho La col. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

According to recent reports, on their latest foray, the team reached 6,400m. “We climbed approximately twelve 60m pitches over rock, snow, and ice of moderate difficulty,” stated Vasiliev.

He noted that on the way to the West Shoulder, they found traces of previous expeditions, including old ropes and snow anchors.

As for the terrain ahead of them, Vasiliev noted:.

From our highest point reached, the terrain ahead looks manageable. We can see two more steep rock steps, each approximately 100m high, along with possible bypasses on steep snow slopes. Beyond these obstacles, the terrain appears easier, and we hope to be able to move simultaneously.

Rocky section on the way to Everest’s West Ridge. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Vasiliev and his team are confident they can manage this route, despite doing so in increasingly wintry conditions.

The route linking the Lho La, the West Shoulder, and the West Ridge of Everest has been completed only twice. A Yugoslavian team led by Tone Skarja did the first complete ascent in 1979. They used the Hornbein Couloir variation on their descent.

It has been revealed that the only repetition was done by a Bulgarian team in 1984. Hristo Prodanov reached the summit on his own and retraced his steps down the ridge but never made it back alive. Some of his partners who summited days later descended via the normal route. Three other teams who climbed the West Shoulder-West Ridge summited by traversing to the North Face, on the Chinese side, and climbing the Hornbein Couloir.

According to recent reports, the North Face of Everest from the West Shoulder. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Industry observers note that objectively speaking, the Hornbein Couloir offers more summit (and survival) chances than the upper part of the West Ridge. However, it requires traversing into Chinese territory. The Russian team has a permit to climb only from Nepal. It is unclear if a brief border trespass could be considered, and Vasiliev has not confirmed what they will do. “First we need to complete one more rotation,” he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that spend your first day at a new job meeting people, not hunting for documents. The night before, gather your bank details for direct deposit and the documents that prove you can work in the U.S. Once you’re there, ask your manager what success looks like in your first 90 days.

Expect three forms by day one, and each needs something only you can supply. One proves you can work in the U.S., one sets up direct deposit, and the third, a W-4, sets how much federal income tax comes out of each paycheck.

The first, Form I-9, has a deadline. Your employer has three business days from your first day to examine your documents, and it may let you go if they’re missing. A U.S. passport is enough on its own. Otherwise, pair an ID such as a driver’s license with your Social Security card or birth certificate, or pick another pair from the list of acceptable documents. Bring originals that haven’t expired, since photocopies don’t count. For a lost one, bring the receipt showing you’ve applied to replace it.

Then settle the rest the night before:.

A latest hire who brings her passport and a voided check can finish the paperwork in ten minutes and spend the rest of the morning meeting the team.

On day one, arrive a few minutes early, write down names as you meet people, and take notes on how work gets done. Then ask your manager what success looks like in your first 90 days.

According to recent reports, you don’t have to pick your benefits on day one, but the window to enroll is often 30 days from your start. Missing it usually means waiting for open enrollment, which comes once a year at most employers. Find your deadline and put it on your calendar before you leave.

  • Recent findings suggest that the winning image highlights bubbling globules of black ink being injected onto a piece of paper by an inkjet printer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since 1975, Nikon’s Small World competition has featured images produced by optical microscopes, an art that usually stays in scientific papers and textbooks. But through the carefully engineered lenses of the microscope, photomicrographers sometimes capture glimpses of strikingly surreal, alien beauty. The 2026 Photomicrography Competition winners include subjects both living and mechanical, small and very small.

The fruiting bodies of a Hemitrichia slime mold remind one distinctly of Dr. Seuss. Photo: Eric Epstein/Nikon Small World.

Recent findings suggest that the winning image highlights bubbling globules of black ink being injected onto a piece of paper by an inkjet printer. Behind the lens was 25-year-old German design student Ole Bielfeldt, whose work explores the surprising complexity of everyday objects. His process is largely DIY: Bielfeldt builds his own setups, cobbles together parts, and learns techniques online.

“I just pick somewhere to start and go for it,” Bielfeldt explained. “You’re likely going to fail at first, and that’s what makes it even more interesting.”.

The experimentation and imperfection, he added, are the most interesting parts of the process and, ultimately, more crucial to him than achieving the highest image quality.

Photo: Ole Bielfeldt/Nikon Small World.

Recent findings suggest that ah, mice; the humble martyrs to scientific progress. A significant amount of science seems to involve cutting up mice and learning from the result. But in this sort of photography, even the strongest mouse advocate must admit that the results are visually spectacular.

It has been revealed that satu Paavonsalo and Dr. Sinem Karaman of the University of Helsinki took this image of a mouse’s eye while researching drug therapy. Photo: Satu Paavonsalo and Dr. Sinem Karaman/Nikon Small World.

Third place went to another rodent part: a 5X-magnified image of neurons in a mouse’s brain.

Photo: Kaelin Wulf and Rachel Flannery/Nikon Small World.

Industry observers note that in defense of humanity, we were also willing to subject our own body parts to photographic investigation. The 7th-place winner came from Dr. Bruno Cisterna and Dr. Eric Vitriol at the Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University. Using confocal imaging, which involves scanning a specimen to generate optical sections, they captured human neurons at 20X magnification.

Industry observers note that these human neurons were grown from reprogrammed skin cells. Photo: Dr. Bruno Cisterna and Dr. Eric Vitriol/Nikon Small World.

Industry observers note that I’ll end with a personal favorite of mine, John-Oliver Dum’s image of a little jumping spider, dusted with pollen. Dum, who won second place, credits a childhood bite for his fascination with spiders. The pollen was cultivated by his wife, specifically to create images like this one.

Recent findings suggest that you can disagree, but I think this little guy is adorable. Photo: John-Oliver Dum.

You can view the full gallery of winners and honorable mentions here. If you want to see photos of larger things, check out the winners from the Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026, Aerial Photography, 2026 Ocean Photographer of the Year, or Memorial Maria Luisa International Photo and Video competitions.

College Students Found Dead After Hiking Colorado Mountain

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the two young men who set off into Colorado’s Sawatch Mountains this month were both passionate about taking the outdoors seriously.
  • But both of them were found dead Wednesday, under circumstances that remain unclear.
  • The bodies were finally discovered near West Apostle Mountain on October 28, just outside of Gunnison, Colorado.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the two young men who set off into Colorado’s Sawatch Mountains this month were both passionate about taking the outdoors seriously. One was studying to be a wildland firefighter, while the other hoped to become a mountain guide.

But both of them were found dead Wednesday, under circumstances that remain unclear. Local authorities spent days looking for missing hikers Kaden Matsuda, 19, and Jackson Donlon, 20.

The bodies were finally discovered near West Apostle Mountain on October 28, just outside of Gunnison, Colorado.

Matsuda and Donlon, students at Colorado Mountain College in Leadville, had planned on hiking and camping near Ice Mountain, a 13,960-foot peak located about 50 miles from Gunnison.

They left for their trip on Oct. 23. College staff notified local authorities they were missing on Oct. 26, according to the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office. The men’s families mentioned they were both experienced hikers.

Matsuda was studying to be a wildland firefighter, and Donlon was training to become a mountain guide.

Recent findings suggest that kaden Matsuda, left, and Jackson Donlon. Supplied: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Kaden Matsuda, left, and Jackson Donlon. Supplied: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Search-and-rescue teams were deployed and found their vehicle at the trailhead. Weather conditions looked risky, with heavy snow falling in Chaffee County.

“Ice Mountain is a very technical climb, and it is recommended that hikers be very experienced when trying to tackle it. That is when it is dry. Although there was only about eight inches of snow around Kaden’s vehicle and in the lower basin, Ice Mountain received one to two feet of snow,” the sheriff’s office noted in a Facebook post.

Multiple local SAR teams worked on the case. Photo: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Multiple local SAR teams worked on the case. Photo: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

Rescue teams used drones, helicopters, and dogs to search for the two hikers. On October 27, they located their tent, which had collapsed under the weight of the snow, near West Apostle Mountain (13,597 feet). Inside were sleeping bags, stoves, and other equipment, but the two men were nowhere to be found.

Sources indicate that the next day, authorities announced they had found their bodies in the mountain’s basin. Officials declined to share potential causes of death, beyond stating that they did not suspect foul play.

Sources indicate that the Sawatch Range of the Rocky Mountains is home to many 13,000- and 14,000-foot peaks. Some of them, like West Apostle Mountain, require technical climbing ability and become substantially more difficult and dangerous during wet weather. The route up the mountain requires traversing fields of loose boulder scree and talus that can be hazardous after snow.

Recent findings suggest that from 2010 to 2017, eight people have died in the Sawatch Mountains. Falls are the most common cause of fatalities for those tackling Colorado’s 13ers and 14ers, as the state’s highest mountains are known to locals.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Part of a rock spire known as a fairy chimney collapsed yesterday near the entrance to one of Turkey’s most popular tourist destinations, killing three people and injuring five others.
  • The incident occurred around 3:15 pm local time in the town of Goreme, in central Turkey’s Cappadocia region yesterday.
  • Industry observers note that rescue teams initially recovered two bodies from the rubble before discovering a third victim overnight, bringing the death toll to three.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Part of a rock spire known as a fairy chimney collapsed yesterday near the entrance to one of Turkey’s most popular tourist destinations, killing three people and injuring five others.

The incident occurred around 3:15 pm local time in the town of Goreme, in central Turkey’s Cappadocia region yesterday. Rocks broke away and fell onto people near the parking area. The site is part of a UNESCO World Heritage landscape, famous for its cave dwellings and cone-shaped rock formations. Nevsehir Governor Huseyin Kok stated that heavy rainfall triggered a landslide that caused the rocks to detach from the formation, according to Reuters.

Industry observers note that rescue teams initially recovered two bodies from the rubble before discovering a third victim overnight, bringing the death toll to three. The deceased include two Turkish citizens and one foreign national. Five others were injured in the collapse. Some of them were later discharged from hospital, according to AFP.

Recent findings suggest that eyewitnesses described a loud noise followed by a large dust cloud. The area was closed to the public, and search operations concluded overnight under floodlights.

Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said an investigation by the chief prosecutor’s office, along with expert assessments, would begin. The collapse occurred on Turkey’s Republic Day, a public holiday when visitor numbers were high.

Cappadocia, in central Anatolia, is renowned for its distinctive fairy chimneys. These tall, thin spires of soft volcanic rock topped by harder caps were shaped over millions of years by wind and water erosion. The Goreme Open-Air Museum and surrounding sites were put on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1985 for their blend of natural landforms and human history, including Byzantine rock-cut churches and underground settlements. The region’s soft rock is geologically fragile and prone to weathering and occasional rockfalls, particularly after heavy rain.

Turkish authorities have previously carried out restoration and monitoring work to address erosion and climate-related risks, and smaller non-fatal collapses were recorded in the area in 2024 and 2025. The site remains one of Turkey’s most visited destinations, drawing tourists for hot-air balloon rides, hiking, and exploration of its unique geology and heritage.

  • Mikel Zabalza, Ruben Perez, and Mikel Saez de Urabain have completed the first ascent of 6,518m Jugal II.
  • According to recent reports, according to Spanish media, the team climbed via the east-southeast side and reached the summit on October 26.
  • In a recent development, jugal II was also the planned goal for Italians Nives Meroi and Romano Benet, who left for the area three weeks ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Zabalza, Ruben Perez, and Mikel Saez de Urabain have completed the first ascent of 6,518m Jugal II.

According to recent reports, according to Spanish media, the team climbed via the east-southeast side and reached the summit on October 26. One day later, they returned to base camp, their home team told Diario de Navarra. Zabalza and Urabain had explored the area in the spring of 2024, but bad weather prevented them from attempting the peak. The team will share more details when they’re back home.

In a recent development, jugal II was also the planned goal for Italians Nives Meroi and Romano Benet, who left for the area three weeks ago. Originally, the team wanted to climb Tilicho Peak in the Annapurna region. Recent storms and floods had cut trails and swept away bridges in that area, so they had to seek an alternative.

ExplorersWeb caught up with Meroi as she and Benet reached a lodge to seek shelter from the heavy rain.

“We’re on our way to Kathmandu, and we are with the Spaniards,” she confirmed. As Nives explained, they all attempted the climb, and the Spanish team reached the summit, while the Italians retreated on the previous day. Until now, there has been no news from the Italians since Tine Cuder of Slovenia, the third team member, fell ill and left the expedition two weeks ago.

It has been revealed that left to right, Nives Meroi, Tine Cuder, and Romano Benet in Kathmandu. Photo: Romano Benet.

It has been revealed that the Jugal Himal is just northeast of Kathmandu, on the Tibetan border. Surprisingly accessible for a previously unclimbed peak, it’s reachable by bus and a few days’ trekking. Jugal I and II opened to foreign expeditions in 2023. In spring 2024, veteran South Korean climber Um Hong-gil led a Korean-Nepalese expedition featuring Sherpa celebrities Dawa Yangzum and Lakpa Dendi to both unclimbed Jugals. They successfully summited Jugal I, but not Jugal II. According to The Himalayan Database, Jugal II remained unclimbed.

The main peaks in Jugal Himal. Photo: Nepali News Hub.

#161015. Tech Report: How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

Tech Report: How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

📅 07 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon.
  • You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.
  • I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun fresh way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which stated something like,.

“Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

“Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

Recent findings suggest that okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

So I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

Sources indicate that one of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

Sources indicate that but occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

Recent findings suggest that I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

Industry observers note that I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

In a recent development, then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

During the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

But eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

Industry observers note that admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

It has been revealed that then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

Industry observers note that it dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

Sources indicate that it reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

According to recent reports, experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning new things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

Sources indicate that one interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

So I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

Thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

Industry observers note that so here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

And of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

But I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

According to recent reports, as with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

It has been revealed that we will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

*(Vine Gold is not all that useful as it turns out as 99.9% of the available items seem to be the same trinkets you see in the Silver tier).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The recent 2026 edition of the Piolets d’Or awards, held last week in a remote corner of the French Alps, felt like an organization trying to adapt to fast-changing times and attract larger audiences while keeping its prestige and spirit intact.
  • In a recent development, explorersWeb was there to meet old acquaintances and to put a face to some of the names we wrote about in the last 12 months.
  • According to recent reports, views of Les Ecrins Massif from Saint-Christophe-en-Oisans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The recent 2026 edition of the Piolets d’Or awards, held last week in a remote corner of the French Alps, felt like an organization trying to adapt to fast-changing times and attract larger audiences while keeping its prestige and spirit intact.

In a recent development, explorersWeb was there to meet old acquaintances and to put a face to some of the names we wrote about in the last 12 months. We also wanted to participate in the collective exercise of reflection about the future.

According to recent reports, views of Les Ecrins Massif from Saint-Christophe-en-Oisans. Photo: Angela Benavides.

Sources indicate that piolet d’Or recipients enjoyed a relaxed atmosphere at the tiny village of Saint-Christophe-en-Oisans and a ceremony at Burg d’Oisans, a 30-minute drive down the valley. Yet, the most interesting event took place the following day, as an elite group of climbers sat around a table in a small hall with large glass windows facing autumn-colored forests and the ragged peaks of the Ecrins Massif, covered in the first snow dust of the season.

According to recent reports, representing the awardees were Nicolas Jean (awarded for climbing Jannu East with Benjamin Vedrines); the complete teams from Ultar Shar, Aikache Chokk, and Jerupaja Grande; a hyper-energetic, widely smiling Peter Habeler, 84, who received a lifetime achievement Piolet d’Or; Simon Welfringer, who gave a talk; organizers Christian Trommsdorf and David Chambre; geographer and chronicler Rodolphe Popier, and two members of the jury: Jordi Corminas of Spain and Paul Ramsden of the UK. At a press conference, these experts debated some of the hot problems in today’s mountaineering.

Sources indicate that simon Welfringer of France speaks at the post-Piolets d’Or experts’ panel. Photo: Angela Benavides.

Trommsdorf noted that the jury had an easy time selecting the awarded climbs this year. He explained how these expert jurists choose the best alpine-style activities of the year.

The members work remotely, choosing from a Big List of outstanding activities. This list is previously compiled by Lindsay Griffin, long-time editor of the American Alpine Journal, and the UK’s Alpine Club. Jurors study the climbs and narrow it down to a short list of candidates, which is not made public. The awards go to those activities chosen by the majority of jury members. In this case, decisions were finalized on the first vote, with no need for a tie-break.

Industry observers note that left to right, Rodolphe Popier, Jordi Corominas, Paul Ramsden (speaking), and David Chambre. Photo: Piotr Drozdz.

That led to the first topic of debate: It was noted that some climbing teams happily announce themselves as “Piolet d’Or nominates” on social media when their climbs appear on the Big List — although organizers make it clear that not all activities on that list are suitable for a Piolet d’Or. Yet, no one supported the idea of making the short lists public. The general agreement was to keep the small “best of the year” finalists available only to the jury.

Sources indicate that the second topic for debate was the presence of a relatively upcoming piece of technology now ubiquitous on expeditions: drones. These have become essential on rescues, but climbing teams also use them to scout the route ahead. In the near future, drones could also carry supplies, emergency kits, or extra equipment. Commercial outfitters are already using them in this way.

Benjamin Vedrines and Nicolas Jean of France used drones to check the state of their planned route on Jannu. However, they explained that the drone was useless in relaying information about a section that they couldn’t see from Base Camp. It had a different angle of view, and the drone lost connection when it tried to approach that area.

It has been revealed that drones piloted by their base camp film crew also hovered overhead as they traversed the long summit ridge. Finally, before the summit push, they used drones to clearly identify the highest point, to make sure they reached the true summit.

The Ultar Sar team also had a drone, they noted. All the awarded climbers agreed that drones are okay as long as the climbers are completely transparent about what they used them for. Jordi Corominas said the drones are a technological innovation that has come to stay, no different than InReach devices, satphones, or even ice axes and crampons.

Jordi Corominas, left, discusses past climbs with Benjamin Vedrines. Photo: Piotr Drozdz.

Interestingly, one jurist stood against the tide: Paul Ramsden is an advocate for the pure alpine-style criteria of the UK climbing school, and with five Piolets d’Or, he is the overall record holder of these prestigious awards. In his opinion, drones spoil the adventure and uncertainty inherent in pure alpine style. Ramsden himself uses neither drones, trackers, nor even satphones.

Industry observers note that finally, Trommsdor suggested possibly expanding the awards to create a special Piolet d’Or for the best rock climb and perhaps even the best ski descent. The idea expand on the new performance category introduced this year in the major list as a test. The category featured, among others, the two Everest ski descents in 2025. Both were heavily supported, and Jim Morrison‘s descent of the Hornbein Couloir was oxygen-assisted.

In the end, one of the performance ski descents received the female award: Typhaine Duperier‘s alpine-style climb+ski descent of Nanga Parbat’s Schell route, with Boris Langenstein.

According to recent reports, it is unclear whether the latest additions will become official in the near future, but some attendees expressed concern about the context in which these take place. Would they award ski expeditions for their boldness or technical excellence without bearing in mind how the skiers reached the start of their descent (supported climbs, fixed routes, even helicopters)?

As for rock climbs: where to set the difference between a rock climb and an alpine climb on high, but dry, faces? The debate was left open. We will find out what, if anything, changes in the next edition of the Piolets d’Or.

According to recent reports, buried houses at the now abandoned village of La Berarde. Photo: Piotr Drozdz.

Industry observers note that the physical award is no longer an actual piolet (ice axe). In the last few years, it has been a hand-crafted trophy that changes with the venue. This time, it was a plaque with a reproduction of Ecrins National Park’s most distinctive peak, La Meige. It rested on a piece of rock from the remains of La Berarde, a nearby village destroyed in a flood two years ago.

According to recent reports, at the Piolets d’Or ceremony in Burg d’Oisans. Photo: Angela Benavides.

It has been revealed that next year, the Piolets d’Or will be staged in the same location, perhaps in late summer. The event will commemorate the 150th anniversary of the first ascent of La Meige. The long-term proposal is to turn the Piolet d’Or ceremony into a bigger, international mountain festival.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if a relative or friend has stopped repaying money you lent them, ask privately for a payment blueprint they can afford, with a set amount and start date.
  • Without a set payment or due date, repaying a loan is easy to put off, and every month of silence makes the subject harder to raise.
  • So skip the hints and make one specific request.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if a relative or friend has stopped repaying money you lent them, ask privately for a payment blueprint they can afford, with a set amount and start date. Confirm it in a text they answer. Save a demand letter or small claims court for a broken plan, or forgive the rest and say so.

Without a set payment or due date, repaying a loan is easy to put off, and every month of silence makes the subject harder to raise.

So skip the hints and make one specific request. Call or meet in private. A text is easy to ignore, and with others listening, embarrassment can turn into an argument. Propose an amount and a schedule they can actually meet. A sister owed $2,400 might ask her brother for $100 a month starting next payday, which clears the debt in two years.

Recent findings suggest that afterward, text them a short summary of the proposal and ask them to confirm it. Their reply is a written record that they owe the money and agreed to repay it, which matters if the plan falls apart.

According to recent reports, if payments don’t start, or start and then stop, put the request in writing. Send a short letter or email that states what they owe, the payments they missed, a deadline to pay, and that you’ll file in small claims court if they don’t. Keep a copy. California’s courts require you to ask for the money before you file, and your copy reveals the judge you did.

Once the deadline passes, file in small claims court. It takes claims up to a cap your state sets, from $2,500 in Kentucky to $25,000 in Delaware and Tennessee. Filing is cheap. California’s fee for a $2,400 claim is $50. For the hearing, bring the bank or payment app record of the transfer and every message in which they agreed to repay you.

In a recent development, suing a relative or friend can cost you the relationship, win or lose. When the relationship matters more than the money, forgive the rest on purpose and tell them it’s now a gift, which settles the debt for both of you. Then stop lending to that person. For anyone else, lend only money you could afford to give away.

The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

Adventurer to Climb 100 Peaks on 2,000Km Taiwan Traverse

📅 31 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that tomorrow, November 1, Japanese adventurer Yoki Tanaka begins a four-month, 2,000km trek north to south down the length of Taiwan.
  • Industry observers note that taiwan has about 268 peaks exceeding 3,000m, but only 100 of them made this special list, which is based not only on height but beauty, difficulty, prominence, and character.
  • Yoki Tanaka arrives in Taiwan earlier this week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that tomorrow, November 1, Japanese adventurer Yoki Tanaka begins a four-month, 2,000km trek north to south down the length of Taiwan. Along the way, he will summit all 100 of Taiwan’s celebrated Baiyue peaks.

Industry observers note that taiwan has about 268 peaks exceeding 3,000m, but only 100 of them made this special list, which is based not only on height but beauty, difficulty, prominence, and character. Prominent Taiwanese mountaineers compiled the list in the early 1970s, partly inspired by Japan’s own list of 100 revered mountains.

Yoki Tanaka arrives in Taiwan earlier this week. Photo: Yoki Tanaka/Instagram.

The 43-year-old Tanaka has specialized in this unusual combination of long-distance trekking and mountaineering. In 2014, he summited Japan’s 100 famous mountains while walking 7,800km over 208 days. (Japan, though far bigger than Taiwan, has only 23 mountains over 3,000m.) A year later, he extended that by climbing 200 mountains and walking 8,000km in 222 days. Finally, he increased that again to 300 mountains. This time, it took him three years and about 20,000km of walking.

Tanaka’s projected route across Taiwan.

Tanaka will begin on Sunday from the northernmost tip of Taiwan, at the Cape Fugui lighthouse, and finish sometime in March at Eluanbi, the country’s southernmost point. The first 150km will be along roads before he reaches his first trailhead. He’ll spend the next week trekking. His first five peaks will be Xueshan (3,886m), Nanhudashan (3,742m), Hehuanshan (3,417m), Qilaishan (3,560m), and Nenggaoshan 3,262m).

Sources indicate that although he won’t use motorized transport for the entire journey, he will have ample opportunity to resupply along the way. His expedition plan includes a charmingly precise breakdown of how he plans to spend his evenings: town stays, 48 days; mountain huts, 38 days; tent camping, 39 days. He has also budgeted 16 rest days and 20 contingency days.

Recent findings suggest that tanaka trains in Taiwan earlier this year. Photo: Yoki Tanaka/Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that his most difficult section, scheduled for early January, will take him through the remote interior of the Central Mountain Range for over two weeks. During this time, he’ll have to carry his own food, search for trails that may no longer exist, and gamble that he will be able to find enough water.

During a December 2025 reconnaissance trip to Xueshan, Taiwan’s second-highest mountain, Tanaka discovered how difficult it can be to obtain water. Two water sources marked on his map were completely dry.

Recent findings suggest that on a previous hike. Photo: Yoki Tanaka/Instagram.

By late January, the Japanese trekker should reach the historic Batongguan Trail, eventually leading to 3,952m Yushan, Taiwan’s highest mountain. The Batongguan Trail was originally constructed in 1875 under the Qing dynasty to establish a route across the mountainous interior. Decades later, Japanese colonial authorities constructed a separate crossing through the region. Sections of the route survive as remote hiking trails and provide access to some of Taiwan’s highest mountains.

According to recent reports, tanaka first visited Taiwan in the spring of 2025 and has made several reconnaissance visits since, including an east-west crossing of the island earlier this year. He had intended to begin his Taiwan 100 Peaks Traverse project this past spring, but local mountaineers advised him to avoid the rainy season and typhoon risks. Their advice prompted him to shift his starting date to November.

Yoki Tanaka on a training hike in Taiwan. Photo: Yoki Tanaka/Instagram.

Interestingly, of Taiwan’s 100 Baiyue peaks, only 99 are now recognized as surpassing 3,000m. The exception is Lushan at 2,981m. It was originally measured at 3,043m but subsequent measurements reduced its elevation. Nevertheless, it remains on the list.

Taiwan’s representative in Japan told Japanese media that the fastest prior completion of the Baiyue by a foreign climber took three years and eight months, spread over multiple trips.

Once Tanaka begins, his expedition website will provide live tracking of his progress across Taiwan.

College students have a lot on their plate already, including the need to study to get good grades, participating in any number of on-campus activities and potentially working part-time to have some spending money.

That said, college students should also focus on their financial future, including steps they can take to build credit before they enter the workforce.

After all, having a credit history and a good credit score can mean being able to rent an apartment, finance a car or take out a loan, whereas having no credit at all can mean sitting on the sidelines until the situation changes.

Fortunately, there are all kinds of ways for young adults to build credit while they’re still in school. Some strategies require a little work on their part, but many are hands-off tasks that you only have to do once.

Make sure your student knows the basic cornerstones of credit building, including the factors that are used to determine credit scores. While factors like new credit, length of credit history and credit mix will play a role in their credit later on, the two most important issues for credit newcomers to focus on include payment history and credit utilization.

Payment history makes up 35% of FICO scores and credit utilization ratio makes up 30% of scores.

Sources indicate that generally speaking, college students and everyone else can score well in these categories by making all bill payments on time and keeping debt levels low. How low?

Industry observers note that most experts recommend keeping credit utilization below 30% at a maximum and below 10% for the best possible results. This means trying to owe less than $300 for every $1,000 in available credit limits at a maximum, but preferably less than $100 for every $1,000 in credit limits.

One step you can personally take to help a child build credit is adding them to your credit card account as an authorized user. This means they will get a credit card in their name and access to your spending limit, but you are legally responsible for any charges they make. Obviously, this move works best when you have excellent credit and a strong history of on-time payments and you proposal to continue using credit responsibly .

While this step can be risky if you’re worried your college student will use their card to overspend, you don’t actually have to give them their physical authorized user credit card.

Sources indicate that in fact, they can get credit for your on-time payments whether they have access to a card or not. If you do decide to give them their credit card, you can do so with the agreement they can only use it for emergency expenses.

In a recent development, your child can build credit faster if they apply for a credit card and get approved for one on their own, yet this can be difficult for students who have no credit history. That noted, secured credit cards require a refundable cash deposit as collateral are very easy to get approved for.

Some secured credit cards like the Ambition Card by College Ave even offer cash back1 on every purchase and don’t charge interest2. If your child opts to start building credit with a secured credit card, make sure they understand the best ways to build credit promptly — keeping credit utilization low and paying bills early or on time each month.

Sources indicate that while secured credit cards are a good option for students with little to no credit get started on their journey to good credit, there are also credit cards specifically designed for college students. Student credit cards are unsecured cards, meaning they don’t require an upfront cash deposit as collateral, but charge interest on any purchases not paid in full each month.

Many student credit cards offer rewards for spending with no annual fee required as well, although these cards do tend to come with a high APR. The key to getting the most out of a student credit card is having your dependent use it only for purchases they can afford and paying off the balance in its entirety each billing cycle. After all, sky high interest rates don’t really matter when you never carry a balance from one month to the next.

“One of the safest ways for college student to build their credit by learning valuable money skills.”.

While secured cards and student credit cards help young adults build credit with each bill payment they make, other payments they’re making can also help.

In fact, using an app like Experian Boost can help them get credit for utility bills they’re paying, subscriptions they pay for and even rent payments they’re making. This app is also free to use, and you only have to set up most bill payments in the app once to have them reported to the credit bureaus.

Industry observers note that there are also rent-specific apps and tools students can use to get credit for rent payments, although they come with fees. Examples include websites like Rental Kharma and RentReporters.

The Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) also notes that students can start building credit with their student loans during school, even if they’re not officially required to make payments until six months after graduation with federal student loans.

Their advice is to make interest-only payments on federal student loans along with payments on any private student loans they have during college in order to start having those payments reported to the credit bureaus as soon as possible.

“Making interest-only payments as a student will not only positively affect your credit history but will also keep the interest from capitalizing and adding to your student loan balance,” the agency writes.

Industry observers note that of course, interest capitalization on loans would only be an issue with private student loans and  Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loans since the U.S. Department of Education pays the interest on Direct Subsidized Loans while you’re in school at least half-time, for six months after you graduate and during periods of deferment.

College students don’t have to wait until they’re done with school to start building credit for the future, and it makes sense to start building positive credit habits early on regardless. Tools like a credit card can help students on their way, whether they opt for a secured credit card or a student card. Other steps like using credit-building apps can also help, and with little effort on the student’s part or on yours.

Either way, the best time to start building credit was a few years ago, and the second best time is now. You can give your student a leg up on the future by helping them build credit so it’s there when they need it.
